group: getInstance without customizer – null version flag

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchemaFactory instance that uses the library's default SpecVersion (currently V7). No exception is thrown.
cases.description: When the version flag is null the method should fall back to the default schema version and still return a usable factory.

group: getInstance without customizer – explicit version flags

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchemaFactory instance configured for Draft‑04 (VersionFlag.V4). The factory should be able to load a Draft‑04 meta‑schema (e.g., getMetaSchema("http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#") returns a non‑null JsonMetaSchema).
cases.description: Pass a concrete version flag (V4) and verify that the returned factory is set up for that version.

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchemaFactory instance configured for Draft‑06 (VersionFlag.V6). The factory should be able to load a Draft‑06 meta‑schema (e.g., getMetaSchema("http://json-schema.org/draft-06/schema#") returns a non‑null JsonMetaSchema).
cases.description: Pass a concrete version flag (V6) and verify that the returned factory is set up for that version.

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchemaFactory instance configured for Draft‑07 (VersionFlag.V7). The factory should be able to load a Draft‑07 meta‑schema (e.g., getMetaSchema("http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#") returns a non‑null JsonMetaSchema).
cases.description: Pass a concrete version flag (V7) and verify that the returned factory is set up for that version.

group: getInstance with customizer – indirect branch verification

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchemaFactory instance where a customizer supplied via the overloaded getInstance(VersionFlag, Consumer) has been applied. For example, if the customizer sets a custom URI loader, the resulting factory should use that loader (verified by calling factory.getSchemaLoader() and checking the custom behaviour).
cases.description: Although the focal method itself does not receive a customizer, it delegates to the two‑argument overload. This test invokes the overload with a non‑null customizer to ensure the branch that applies the customizer is exercised.

group: getInstance without customizer – newer draft versions

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchemaFactory instance configured for Draft‑2019‑09 (VersionFlag.V2019_09). Calling factory.getMetaSchema("https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema#") returns a non‑null JsonMetaSchema whose version matches V2019_09.
cases.description: Verify that the factory correctly recognises the 2019‑09 draft flag and can load its meta‑schema.

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchemaFactory instance configured for Draft‑2020‑12 (VersionFlag.V2020_12). Calling factory.getMetaSchema("https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema#") returns a non‑null JsonMetaSchema whose version matches V2020_12.
cases.description: Verify that the factory correctly recognises the 2020‑12 draft flag and can load its meta‑schema.

group: getInstance caching behavior – same version returns same instance

cases.expected: Two consecutive calls to JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(VersionFlag.V6) return the *exact same* object reference (instance). No new objects are created, confirming internal caching.
cases.description: Ensures that the factory caches instances per version flag and re‑uses them.

group: getInstance caching behavior – different versions return different instances

cases.expected: The objects returned by JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(V4) and JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(V7) are not the same reference (they are distinct instances).
cases.description: Confirms that caching is scoped to the version flag and does not mistakenly return a single shared instance for all versions.

group: getInstance overload with null customizer – indirect branch verification

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchemaFactory instance identical to the one returned by the single‑argument overload. No customisation occurs and no exception is thrown.
cases.description: Calls the two‑argument overload with a null Consumer to verify that the method correctly forwards to the single‑argument path without applying any customisation.
